title: The year of the elephant
hookLine: an army with an elephant marches on the Ka'ba and is turned back, in the year the Prophet ﷺ is born

lines: THE MECCANS HEAD FOR THE HILLS.
cards: Over the hills south of Mecca comes an army. Soldiers, banners, dust. At the front, an elephant: a living mountain, walking.

The army has come for one reason, to tear down the Ka'ba. Its commander, Abraha, governor of Yemen, had built a grand house of worship in his own city, and he wanted the pilgrims of Arabia to go there instead.
So he's come to knock down the competition. The Meccans are traders, not soldiers. They look at the elephant, and they head for the hills.

teach.b: The early biography of the Prophet, by Ibn Ishaq, tells what happened next.
Abraha's soldiers seize two hundred camels belonging to the chief of Mecca, an old man named 'Abd al-Muttalib. 'Abd al-Muttalib goes to meet Abraha, and Abraha is impressed by this dignified man.
Surely he's come to plead for the Ka'ba. But he asks only for his camels. Abraha is disappointed: you came about camels, and not the house of your fathers' religion?
The old man answers, in the words the story remembers: I am the owner of the camels. The House has its own Lord, who will protect it.
Then the elephant, the story says, kneels down facing Mecca and will not get up. Turn it toward Yemen, it walks. Turn it toward the Ka'ba, it sits.
The Qur'an tells the rest in a short surah, the hundred and fifth, Al-Fil, the Elephant. In Pickthall's translation it begins: “Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant?”
Allah sent against them, it says, “swarms of flying creatures,” pelting them with stones of baked clay, until they were like chewed-up straw. The army is broken, and the House stands.
Tradition says the Arabs dated years from it: the Year of the Elephant.

teach.h: THE YEAR A BOY IS BORN.
teach.b: And in that same year, Ibn Ishaq says, a boy was born in Mecca into 'Abd al-Muttalib's own family: his grandson. His name was Muhammad ﷺ.
Muslim tradition sees the timing as a sign: the House is protected, and the one who will restore it to the worship of One God is born.

how: Surah Al-Fil is a short surah often recited in prayer; the Year of the Elephant is remembered as the year of the Prophet's birth.

the Qur'an tells of the army of the elephant

Ibn Ishaq places his birth in that year.

games.q: you're 'Abd al-Muttalib, chief of Mecca. an army with an elephant has seized your camels and come to destroy the Ka'ba. you meet its commander. what do you ask for?
games.why: he asks for his camels: I am the owner of the camels; the House has its own Lord, who will protect it (Ibn Ishaq).

practice: If you can, step outside or go to a window, look up, and take one long, slow breath; notice how big it is up there, and how small the things that frighten you look against it.
Then sit wherever you are and let the rest of the time be quiet: you don't have to protect everything yourself. If you pray, you can hand one worry to the Lord of the House.

wordCard.voice: Al-feel, the elephant: the animal at the front of the army that could not be moved to tear down the Ka'ba.

orig.note: Arabic: the elephant; the name of Surah 105.

carryVoice: Your line: the house has an owner. Tomorrow, the boy grows up an orphan. Day seventy-nine, done.
